report.root_cause: A burst of commands over RCON from 127.0.0.1 at about 08:48:53 summoned 386 unnamed pigs, tagged 'mcsre_f', near spawn (around x 0-20, y -60, z -10 to 10). Then commands run as each pig summoned 4 single items (string, stick, rotten flesh, oak log), 1,544 items in total. The tag was removed at 08:48:58. Entity count went from 24 to 1,954. It was a one-time burst and did not keep going. No plugin, datapack (world/datapacks has only the default 'bukkit') or player was involved.
report.actions: 1) Watched the baseline: 24 entities, 20 TPS. 2) Saw entities jump to 1,954 (1,544 items, 387 pigs) and declared the incident. 3) Read the logs: mass summon commands came over RCON, then pig-executed summons of items. Checked world/datapacks: nothing unusual. 4) Confirmed the flood had stopped growing. 5) Told flood pigs apart from the real one: the only named pig is 'Wilbur', the original. The flood items are exactly 386 each of string, stick, rotten flesh and oak log, all count 1. 6) Ran 'kill @e[type=pig,name=Pig]', which killed the 386 unnamed flood pigs; Wilbur was kept. 7) Ran 'kill @e[type=item,nbt={Item:{Count:1b}},nbt=!{Item:{tag:{}}}]', which killed 1,590 items: the 1,544 flood items plus single porkchops dropped by the killed pigs. 8) Ran 'kill @e[type=item,nbt={Item:{id:"minecraft:porkchop"}}]' to clear the remaining 117 porkchop stacks dropped by the killed pigs; I checked first that no other item types were on the ground. 9) Checked for about 60 s: entities back to 24, exactly the baseline (Wilbur, cow, sheep, striders, minecarts, end crystals and armor stand all still there), TPS 20, MSPT under 1.
report.residual_risk: The flood came in over RCON from localhost. If the RCON password or a local process is compromised or misused, it could happen again. Recommend rotating the RCON password and checking which local tools have RCON access. The item kill selector was broad (single, untagged item stacks); I confirmed no non-flood item types were on the ground right before running it.
